o: »No se pasaron quince días, cuando ya nuestro renegado tenía comprada una muy buena barca, capaz de más de treinta personas: y, para asegurar su hecho y dalle color, quiso hacer, como hizo, un viaje a un lugar que se llamaba Sargel, que está treinta leguas de Argel hacia la parte de Orán, en el cual hay mucha contratación de higos pasos.
t: »Fifteen days had not passed when our renegade had already bought a very good boat, capable of carrying more than thirty persons; and, to make good his deed and give it a plausible appearance, he wanted to make, as he did, a voyage to a place called Sargel, which is thirty leagues from Algiers toward Oran, where there is a great trade in dried figs.

o: Dos o tres veces hizo este viaje, en compañía del tagarino que había dicho.
t: He made this voyage two or three times, in company with the Tagarin he had mentioned.

o: Tagarinos llaman en Berbería a los moros de Aragón, y a los de Granada, mudéjares; y en el reino de Fez llaman a los mudéjares elches, los cuales son la gente de quien aquel rey más se sirve en la guerra.
t: In Barbary they call the Moors of Aragon Tagarins, and those of Granada Mudéjares; and in the kingdom of Fez they call the Mudéjares elches, and these are the people of whom that king makes the most use in war.

o: De cristianos cautivos se dejan tratar y comunicar, aun más de aquello que sería razonable; y a mí me hubiera pesado que él la hubiera hablado, que quizá la alborotara, viendo que su negocio andaba en boca de renegados.
t: They allow themselves to be treated and spoken to of Christian captives, even more than would be reasonable; and it would have weighed on me if he had spoken to her, for perhaps he might have stirred her up, seeing that his business was being talked about among renegades.

o: A los cuales no les dije otra cosa, sino que el primer viernes en la tarde se saliesen uno a uno, disimuladamente, y se fuesen la vuelta del jardín de Agi Morato, y que allí me aguardasen hasta que yo fuese.
t: To whom I said nothing else but that on the first Friday, in the afternoon, they should slip out one by one, unnoticed, and take their way back to the garden of Agi Morato, and wait for me there until I came.

o: A cada uno di este aviso de por sí, con orden que, aunque allí viesen a otros cristianos, no les dijesen sino que yo les había mandado esperar en aquel lugar.
t: I gave each of them this warning separately, with the order that even if they saw other Christians there, they should say nothing except that I had ordered them to wait in that place.

o: »Hecha esta diligencia, me faltaba hacer otra, que era la que más me convenía: y era la de avisar a Zoraida en el punto que estaban los negocios, para que estuviese apercebida y sobre aviso, que no se sobresaltase si de improviso la asaltásemos antes del tiempo que ella podía imaginar que la barca de cristianos podía volver.
t: "Once this task was done, there was still another I had to perform, the one most needful for me: to warn Zoraida of the state of affairs, so that she would be on her guard and forewarned, and would not be startled if we should assault her unexpectedly before the time she could imagine the boat of Christians might return."

o: Respondíle que era esclavo de Arnaúte Mamí (y esto, porque sabía yo por muy cierto que era un grandísimo amigo suyo), y que buscaba de todas yerbas, para hacer ensalada.
t: I answered that I was a slave of Arnaut Mamí (and I said so because I knew for a very certain truth that he was a great friend of hers), and that I was searching for all sorts of herbs, to make a salad.

o: Preguntóme, por el consiguiente, si era hombre de rescate o no, y que cuánto pedía mi amo por mí.
t: He then asked me whether I was a ransomed man or not, and how much my master asked for me.

o: »Demasiada cosa sería decir yo agora la mucha hermosura, la gentileza, el gallardo y rico adorno con que mi querida Zoraida se mostró a mis ojos: sólo diré que más perlas pendían de su hermosísimo cuello, orejas y cabellos, que cabellos tenía en la cabeza.
t: "It would be too much to tell now the great beauty, the grace, the gallantry and rich adornment with which my beloved Zoraida appeared before my eyes: I will say only that more pearls hung from her most beautiful neck, ears and hair than she had hairs on her head.

o: En las gargantas de los sus pies, que descubiertas, a su usanza, traía, traía dos carcajes (que así se llamaban las manillas o ajorcas de los pies en morisco) de purísimo oro, con tantos diamantes engastados, que ella me dijo después que su padre los estimaba en diez mil doblas, y las que traía en las muñecas de las manos valían otro tanto.
t: On the insteps of her feet, which she wore bare after her fashion, she had two anklets (which in Moorish are called carcajes, that is, the manillas or anklets of the feet) of purest gold, set with so many diamonds that she told me afterwards her father valued them at ten thousand doubloons, and those she wore on her wrists were worth as much again.

o: Si con todo este adorno podía venir entonces hermosa, o no, por las reliquias que le han quedado en tantos trabajos se podrá conjeturar cuál debía de ser en las prosperidades.
t: If with all this adornment she could come then beautiful, or not, from the remains of her beauty that have survived her hardships, one may conjecture what she must have been in her prosperity.

o: Porque ya se sabe que la hermosura de algunas mujeres tiene días y sazones, y requiere accidentes para diminuirse o acrecentarse; y es natural cosa que las pasiones del ánimo la levanten o abajen, puesto que las más veces la destruyen.
t: For it is well known that the beauty of some women has its days and seasons, and needs accidents to diminish or increase; and it is natural that the passions of the soul should raise or lower it, since most often they destroy it.

o: »Digo, en fin, que entonces llegó en todo estremo aderezada y en todo estremo hermosa, o, a lo menos, a mí me pareció serlo la más que hasta entonces había visto; y con esto, viendo las obligaciones en que me había puesto, me parecía que tenía delante de mí una deidad del cielo, venida a la tierra para mi gusto y para mi remedio.
t: "In short, then, I say that she arrived arrayed in every extreme and beautiful in every extreme, or, at least, she seemed to me more beautiful than any woman I had seen until then; and with this, seeing the obligations I had taken upon myself, it seemed to me that I had before me a divinity from heaven, come down to earth for my pleasure and my cure."

o: Así como ella llegó, le dijo su padre en su lengua como yo era cautivo de su amigo Arnaúte Mamí, y que venía a buscar ensalada.
t: As soon as she arrived, her father told her in his own tongue, as I was a captive of his friend Arnaut Mamí, and that I had come to look for salad.

o: Ella tomó la mano, y en aquella mezcla de lenguas que tengo dicho me preguntó si era caballero y qué era la causa que no me rescataba.
t: She took my hand, and in that mixture of tongues I have mentioned, she asked me whether I was a gentleman, and what was the reason I did not ransom myself.

o: Yo le respondí que ya estaba rescatado, y que en el precio podía echar de ver en lo que mi amo me estimaba, pues había dado por mí mil y quinientos zoltanís.
t: I answered that I was already ransomed, and that in the price she could see how highly my master valued me, since he had given a thousand five hundred zoltanis for me.

o: Desto se riyó muy de veras su padre, y dijo: ''Gualá, cristiano, que debe de ser muy hermosa si se parece a mi hija, que es la más hermosa de todo este reino.
t: At this her father laughed heartily and said: "Gualá, Christian, she must be very beautiful if she takes after my daughter, who is the most beautiful in this whole kingdom.

o: Si no, mírala bien, y verás cómo te digo verdad''.
t: If not, look at her well, and you will see how I tell you the truth."

o: Servíanos de intérprete a las más de estas palabras y razones el padre de Zoraida, como más ladino; que, aunque ella hablaba la bastarda lengua que, como he dicho, allí se usa, más declaraba su intención por señas que por palabras.
t: Zoraida's father served as interpreter for most of these words and speeches, being the more ladino; for though she spoke the bastard tongue that, as I have said, is used there, she declared her intention more by signs than by words.

o: »Estando en estas y otras muchas razones, llegó un moro corriendo, y dijo, a grandes voces, que por las bardas o paredes del jardín habían saltado cuatro turcos, y andaban cogiendo la fruta, aunque no estaba madura.
t: "While we were in these and many other words, a Moor came running and said, in a loud voice, that four Turks had climbed over the walls of the garden and were gathering the fruit, though it was not yet ripe."

o: Sobresaltóse el viejo, y lo mesmo hizo Zoraida, porque es común y casi natural el miedo que los moros a los turcos tienen, especialmente a los soldados, los cuales son tan insolentes y tienen tanto imperio sobre los moros que a ellos están sujetos, que los tratan peor que si fuesen esclavos suyos.
t: The old man was startled, and so was Zoraida, because the fear the Moors feel for the Turks is common and almost natural, especially for the soldiers, who are so insolent and hold such sway over the Moors subject to them that they treat them worse than if they were their own slaves.

o: Digo, pues, que dijo su padre a Zoraida: ''Hija, retírate a la casa y enciérrate, en tanto que yo voy a hablar a estos canes; y tú, cristiano, busca tus yerbas, y vete en buen hora, y llévete Alá con bien a tu tierra''.
t: So, I say, her father said to Zoraida: "Daughter, withdraw to the house and shut yourself in while I go to speak with these dogs; and you, Christian, look for your herbs, and go in God's hour, and may Allah take you safely to your land."

o: Yo me incliné, y él se fue a buscar los turcos, dejándome solo con Zoraida, que comenzó a dar muestras de irse donde su padre la había mandado.
t: I bowed, and he went to seek the Turks, leaving me alone with Zoraida, who began to give signs of withdrawing where her father had sent her.

o: Pero, apenas él se encubrió con los árboles del jardín, cuando ella, volviéndose a mí, llenos los ojos de lágrimas, me dijo: ''Ámexi, cristiano, ámexi''; que quiere decir: "¿Vaste, cristiano, vaste?"
t: But scarcely had he hidden himself among the trees of the garden when she, turning to me with her eyes full of tears, said to me: "Ámexi, cristiano, ámexi"; which means: "Are you going, Christian, are you going?"

o: Yo la respondí: ''Señora, sí, pero no en ninguna manera sin ti: el primero jumá me aguarda, y no te sobresaltes cuando nos veas; que sin duda alguna iremos a tierra de cristianos''.
t: I answered her: "Mistress, yes, but in no way without you: the first Friday I await, and do not be alarmed when you see us; for beyond all doubt we shall go to the land of Christians."

o: Su padre llegó corriendo adonde estábamos, y, viendo a su hija de aquella manera, le preguntó que qué tenía; pero, como ella no le respondiese, dijo su padre: ''Sin duda alguna que con el sobresalto de la entrada de estos canes se ha desmayado''.
t: Her father came running to where we were and, seeing his daughter in that state, asked her what was wrong; but since she did not answer him, her father said: 'No doubt the shock of the arrival of these dogs has made her faint.'

o: Y, quitándola del mío, la arrimó a su pecho; y ella, dando un suspiro y aún no enjutos los ojos de lágrimas, volvió a decir: ''Ámexi, cristiano, ámexi'': "Vete, cristiano, vete".
t: And, taking her from me, he pressed her to his breast; and she, giving a sigh and with her eyes not yet dry of tears, said again: 'Ámexi, cristiano, ámexi': "Go, Christian, go".

o: A lo que su padre respondió: ''No importa, hija, que el cristiano se vaya, que ningún mal te ha hecho, y los turcos ya son idos.
t: To which her father replied: 'It does not matter, daughter, if the Christian goes; he has done you no harm, and the Turks are already gone.

o: »Con esto, me despedí al punto de entrambos; y ella, arrancándosele el alma, al parecer, se fue con su padre; y yo, con achaque de buscar las yerbas, rodeé muy bien y a mi placer todo el jardín: miré bien las entradas y salidas, y la fortaleza de la casa, y la comodidad que se podía ofrecer para facilitar todo nuestro negocio.
t: »With this, I took my leave of them both; and she, seeming to tear her soul away, went off with her father; and I, under the pretense of looking for herbs, walked all around the garden at my leisure and to my satisfaction: I inspected the entrances and exits, the strength of the house, and the comfort it could offer to make easier the whole of our business.

o: Hecho esto, me vine y di cuenta de cuanto había pasado al renegado y a mis compañeros; y ya no veía la hora de verme gozar sin sobresalto del bien que en la hermosa y bella Zoraida la suerte me ofrecía.
t: Having done this, I came back and found out what had happened with the renegade and my companions; and I could no longer wait to enjoy, without alarm, the good fortune that fate offered me in the beautiful and lovely Zoraida.

o: Ya los cristianos que habían de bogar el remo estaban prevenidos y escondidos por diversas partes de todos aquellos alrededores.
t: The Christians who were to row at the oars were already posted and hidden in various places all around those surroundings.

o: Todos estaban suspensos y alborozados, aguardándome, deseosos ya de embestir con el bajel que a los ojos tenían; porque ellos no sabían el concierto del renegado, sino que pensaban que a fuerza de brazos habían de haber y ganar la libertad, quitando la vida a los moros que dentro de la barca estaban.
t: They were all in suspense and excitement, awaiting me, already eager to attack the vessel they had before their eyes; for they did not know the renegade's arrangement, but thought that by force of arms they would have to win and gain their freedom, taking the lives of the Moors who were inside the boat.

o: »Sucedió, pues, que, así como yo me mostré y mis compañeros, todos los demás escondidos que nos vieron se vinieron llegando a nosotros.
t: »It happened, then, that as soon as I showed myself, along with my companions, all the others who were hidden and saw us began to come up to us.

o: Esto era ya a tiempo que la ciudad estaba ya cerrada, y por toda aquella campaña ninguna persona parecía.
t: It was already late, for the city was already closed, and not a single person seemed to be anywhere in that whole countryside.

o: Como estuvimos juntos, dudamos si sería mejor ir primero por Zoraida, o rendir primero a los moros bagarinos que bogaban el remo en la barca.
t: Once we were together, we doubted whether it would be better to go first for Zoraida, or to capture first the Moorish galley-slaves who were rowing in the boat.

o: Y, estando en esta duda, llegó a nosotros nuestro renegado diciéndonos que en qué nos deteníamos, que ya era hora, y que todos sus moros estaban descuidados, y los más dellos durmiendo.
t: And while we were in this doubt, our renegade came up to us, telling us what we were waiting for, that it was already time, and that all his Moors were off their guard, and most of them asleep.

o: Dijímosle en lo que reparábamos, y él dijo que lo que más importaba era rendir primero el bajel, que se podía hacer con grandísima facilidad y sin peligro alguno, y que luego podíamos ir por Zoraida.
t: We told him what we were considering, and he said that what mattered most was to capture the vessel first, which could be done with the greatest ease and without any danger, and that afterwards we could go for Zoraida.

o: Pareciónos bien a todos lo que decía, y así, sin detenernos más, haciendo él la guía, llegamos al bajel, y, saltando él dentro primero, metió mano a un alfanje, y dijo en morisco: ''Ninguno de vosotros se mueva de aquí, si no quiere que le cueste la vida''.
t: What he said seemed good to all of us, and so, without delaying any further, with him as our guide, we reached the vessel, and, he leaping in first, laid hold of an alfange and said in Morisco: 'Not one of you stir from here, unless you want it to cost you your life'.

o: Ya, a este tiempo, habían entrado dentro casi todos los cristianos.
t: By this time, almost all the Christians had already gotten inside.

o: Estaba la bellísima Zoraida aguardándonos a una ventana, y, así como sintió gente, preguntó con voz baja si éramos nizarani, como si dijera o preguntara si éramos cristianos.
t: The most beautiful Zoraida was awaiting us at a window, and, as soon as she sensed people, she asked in a low voice whether we were nizari, as if she said or asked whether we were Christians.

o: Yo le respondí que sí, y que bajase.
t: I answered her that we were, and that she should come down.

o: Cuando ella me conoció, no se detuvo un punto, porque, sin responderme palabra, bajó en un instante, abrió la puerta y mostróse a todos tan hermosa y ricamente vestida que no lo acierto a encarecer.
t: When she knew me, she did not pause a moment, for, without answering me a word, she came down in an instant, opened the door, and showed herself to everyone so beautiful and richly dressed that I cannot adequately praise it.

o: Luego que yo la vi, le tomé una mano y la comencé a besar, y el renegado hizo lo mismo, y mis dos camaradas; y los demás, que el caso no sabían, hicieron lo que vieron que nosotros hacíamos, que no parecía sino que le dábamos las gracias y la reconocíamos por señora de nuestra libertad.
t: As soon as I saw her, I took her hand and began to kiss it, and the renegade did the same, and my two comrades; and the others, who did not know the matter, did as they saw us doing, for it seemed as though we were giving her thanks and acknowledging her as the mistress of our liberty.

o: El renegado le dijo en lengua morisca si estaba su padre en el jardín.
t: The renegade told her in the Moorish tongue whether her father was in the garden.

o: Y, diciendo esto, se volvió a entrar, diciendo que muy presto volvería; que nos estuviésemos quedos, sin hacer ningún ruido.
t: And, saying this, he went back inside, saying that he would return very soon; that we should stay still, making no noise.

o: ¡Ladrones, ladrones!''; por los cuales gritos nos vimos todos puestos en grandísima y temerosa confusión.
t: "Thieves, thieves!"; and because of those shouts we all found ourselves in the greatest and most fearful confusion.

o: Pero el renegado, viendo el peligro en que estábamos, y lo mucho que le importaba salir con aquella empresa antes de ser sentido, con grandísima presteza, subió donde Agi Morato estaba, y juntamente con él fueron algunos de nosotros; que yo no osé desamparar a la Zoraida, que como desmayada se había dejado caer en mis brazos.
t: But the renegade, seeing the danger we were in, and how much it mattered to him to succeed in that enterprise before he was discovered, with very great speed climbed up to where Agi Morato was, and together with him some of us went up; for I did not dare to leave Zoraida, who had dropped, as if faint, into my arms.

o: En resolución, los que subieron se dieron tan buena maña que en un momento bajaron con Agi Morato, trayéndole atadas las manos y puesto un pañizuelo en la boca, que no le dejaba hablar palabra, amenazándole que el hablarla le había de costar la vida.
t: In short, those who went up managed so well that in a moment they came back down with Agi Morato, bringing him with his hands tied and a handkerchief over his mouth, which did not let him speak a word, threatening him that speaking would cost him his life.

o: Cuando su hija le vio, se cubrió los ojos por no verle, y su padre quedó espantado, ignorando cuán de su voluntad se había puesto en nuestras manos.
t: When his daughter saw him, she covered her eyes so as not to look at him, and her father was terrified, not knowing how willingly he had placed himself in our hands.

o: Mas, entonces siendo más necesarios los pies, con diligencia y presteza nos pusimos en la barca; que ya los que en ella habían quedado nos esperaban, temerosos de algún mal suceso nuestro.
t: But then, our feet being more needed, with diligence and speed we set off for the boat; for those who had remained in it were already waiting, fearful of some mishap of ours.

o: »Apenas serían dos horas pasadas de la noche, cuando ya estábamos todos en la barca, en la cual se le quitó al padre de Zoraida la atadura de las manos y el paño de la boca; pero tornóle a decir el renegado que no hablase palabra, que le quitarían la vida.
t: "It was scarcely two hours past nightfall when we were all in the boat, in which the father of Zoraida had his bonds and the cloth taken from his mouth; but the renegade told him again that he was not to speak a word, that they would take his life.

o: Él, como vio allí a su hija, comenzó a suspirar ternísimamente, y más cuando vio que yo estrechamente la tenía abrazada, y que ella sin defender, quejarse ni esquivarse, se estaba queda; pero, con todo esto, callaba, porque no pusiesen en efeto las muchas amenazas que el renegado le hacía.
t: He, as soon as he saw his daughter there, began to sigh most tenderly, and even more when he saw that I was holding her tightly in my arms, and that she, without defending herself, complaining, or avoiding it, was staying still; but with all this, he kept silent, so that they would not put into effect the many threats the renegade made against him.

o: »Pero, a causa de soplar un poco el viento tramontana y estar la mar algo picada, no fue posible seguir la derrota de Mallorca, y fuenos forzoso dejarnos ir tierra a tierra la vuelta de Orán, no sin mucha pesadumbre nuestra, por no ser descubiertos del lugar de Sargel, que en aquella costa cae sesenta millas de Argel.
t: "But, because the tramontane wind was blowing a little and the sea was somewhat choppy, it was not possible to continue the route to Mallorca, and we were forced to go coasting back toward Oran, not without much sorrow on our part, for fear of being discovered from the place of Sargel, which on that coast lies sixty miles from Algiers.

o: Iba Zoraida, en tanto que se navegaba, puesta la cabeza entre mis manos, por no ver a su padre, y sentía yo que iba llamando a Lela Marién que nos ayudase.
t: Zoraida went, while we were sailing, with her head between my hands, so as not to see her father, and I felt that she was calling on Lela Marién to help us.

o: Hízose ansí, y en esto comenzó a soplar un viento largo, que nos obligó a hacer luego vela y a dejar el remo, y enderezar a Orán, por no ser posible poder hacer otro viaje.
t: This happened so, and then a long wind began to blow, which forced us to make sail at once and to leave off rowing, and to head for Oran, since it was not possible to make another voyage.

o: Todo se hizo con muchísima presteza; y así, a la vela, navegamos por más de ocho millas por hora, sin llevar otro temor alguno sino el de encontrar con bajel que de corso fuese.
t: Everything was done with very great speed; and so, under sail, we sailed more than eight miles an hour, with no other fear than that of meeting with some vessel of corsairs.

o: »Dimos de comer a los moros bagarinos, y el renegado les consoló diciéndoles como no iban cautivos, que en la primera ocasión les darían libertad.
t: "We gave food to the captive Moors, and the renegade consoled them by telling them that they were not to be slaves, that at the first opportunity they would be given their freedom.

o: En diciendo esto, comenzó a llorar tan amargamente que a todos nos movió a compasión, y forzó a Zoraida que le mirase; la cual, viéndole llorar, así se enterneció que se levantó de mis pies y fue a abrazar a su padre, y, juntando su rostro con el suyo, comenzaron los dos tan tierno llanto que muchos de los que allí íbamos le acompañamos en él.
t: On saying this, he began to weep so bitterly that he moved all of us to compassion, and he forced Zoraida to look at him; who, seeing him weep, was so moved that she rose from my feet and went to embrace her father, and, joining her face to his, the two of them began such tender weeping that many of us who were there joined in it.

o: Respóndeme a esto, que me tiene más suspenso y admirado que la misma desgracia en que me hallo''.
t: Answer me this, which holds me more suspended and amazed than the very misfortune in which I find myself."

o: »Todo lo que el moro decía a su hija nos lo declaraba el renegado, y ella no le respondía palabra.
t: "Everything the Moor said to his daughter, the renegade interpreted for us, and she did not answer him a word.

o: Pero, cuando él vio a un lado de la barca el cofrecillo donde ella solía tener sus joyas, el cual sabía él bien que le había dejado en Argel, y no traídole al jardín, quedó más confuso, y preguntóle que cómo aquel cofre había venido a nuestras manos, y qué era lo que venía dentro.
t: But, when he saw at one side of the boat the little chest where she used to keep her jewels, which he well knew she had left in Algiers and had not brought to the garden, he was more confused, and asked her how that chest had come into our hands, and what it was that came inside it.

o: »Apenas hubo oído esto el moro, cuando, con una increíble presteza, se arrojó de cabeza en la mar, donde sin ninguna duda se ahogara, si el vestido largo y embarazoso que traía no le entretuviera un poco sobre el agua.
t: "The Moor had scarcely heard this when, with incredible speed, he threw himself headlong into the sea, where without a doubt he would have drowned, had not the long and cumbersome garment he wore held him up a little on the water.

o: Dio voces Zoraida que le sacasen, y así, acudimos luego todos, y, asiéndole de la almalafa, le sacamos medio ahogado y sin sentido, de que recibió tanta pena Zoraida que, como si fuera ya muerto, hacía sobre él un tierno y doloroso llanto.
t: Zoraida cried out that they should pull him out, and so we all ran up at once, and, seizing him by the almalafa, we pulled him out half-drowned and unconscious, at which Zoraida felt such grief that, as if he were already dead, she poured over him a tender and painful weeping.

o: »Pusimos nuestras centinelas en tierra, y no dejamos jamás los remos de la mano; comimos de lo que el renegado había proveído, y rogamos a Dios y a Nuestra Señora, de todo nuestro corazón, que nos ayudase y favoreciese para que felicemente diésemos fin a tan dichoso principio.
t: "We posted our sentinels on shore, and never let the oars out of our hands; we ate of what the renegade had provided, and we prayed to God and to Our Lady, with all our heart, that they would help and favor us so that we might happily bring to a close so auspicious a beginning.

o: Diose orden, a suplicación de Zoraida, como echásemos en tierra a su padre y a todos los demás moros que allí atados venían, porque no le bastaba el ánimo, ni lo podían sufrir sus blandas entrañas, ver delante de sus ojos atado a su padre y aquellos de su tierra presos.
t: At Zoraida's entreaty, orders were given to set ashore her father and all the other Moors who came there bound, because it was not enough for her spirit, nor could her tender heart bear, to see before her eyes her father bound and those of her land in captivity.

o: Prometímosle de hacerlo así al tiempo de la partida, pues no corría peligro el dejallos en aquel lugar, que era despoblado.
t: We promised to do so at the start of the voyage, for there was no danger in leaving them in that place, which was uninhabited.

o: No fueron tan vanas nuestras oraciones que no fuesen oídas del cielo; que, en nuestro favor, luego volvió el viento, tranquilo el mar, convidándonos a que tornásemos alegres a proseguir nuestro comenzado viaje.
t: Our prayers were not so fruitless that they were not heard from heaven; for in our favor the wind soon turned back, the sea grew calm, and invited us to cheerfully resume our begun journey.

o: »Viendo esto, desatamos a los moros, y uno a uno los pusimos en tierra, de lo que ellos se quedaron admirados; pero, llegando a desembarcar al padre de Zoraida, que ya estaba en todo su acuerdo, dijo: ''¿Por qué pensáis, cristianos, que esta mala hembra huelga de que me deis libertad?
t: "Seeing this, we freed the Moors, and one by one we set them ashore, at which they were amazed; but when it came to landing the father of Zoraida, who was already fully resolved, he said: 'Why do you think, Christians, that this wicked woman is glad you give me my freedom?

o: ¿Pensáis que es por piedad que de mí tiene?
t: Do you think it is out of pity that she feels for me?

o: No, por cierto, sino que lo hace por el estorbo que le dará mi presencia cuando quiera poner en ejecución sus malos deseos; ni penséis que la ha movido a mudar religión entender ella que la vuestra a la nuestra se aventaja, sino el saber que en vuestra tierra se usa la deshonestidad más libremente que en la nuestra''.
t: No, certainly not, but because my presence will hinder her whenever she wants to carry out her evil desires; nor think that she has been moved to change her religion by understanding that yours is better than ours, but rather by knowing that in your land dishonesty is practiced more freely than in ours.'

o: Y, volviéndose a Zoraida, teniéndole yo y otro cristiano de entrambos brazos asido, porque algún desatino no hiciese, le dijo: ''¡Oh infame moza y mal aconsejada muchacha!
t: And, turning to Zoraida, while I and another Christian held her fast by both arms, so that she might do nothing rash, he said: 'Oh infamous girl, ill-advised maiden!

o: ¿Adónde vas, ciega y desatinada, en poder destos perros, naturales enemigos nuestros?
t: Where are you going, blind and foolish woman, into the power of these dogs, natural enemies of ours?

o: Alá sabe bien que no pude hacer otra cosa de la que he hecho, y que estos cristianos no deben nada a mi voluntad, pues, aunque quisiera no venir con ellos y quedarme en mi casa, me fuera imposible, según la priesa que me daba mi alma a poner por obra ésta que a mí me parece tan buena como tú, padre amado, la juzgas por mala''.
t: God knows well that I could do nothing other than what I have done, and that these Christians owe nothing to my will; for even if I wished not to come with them and to stay in my house, it would have been impossible for me, such was the eagerness my soul felt to put into effect that deed which seems to me as good as it does to you, beloved father, you judge it as bad'.

o: Esto dijo, a tiempo que ni su padre la oía, ni nosotros ya le veíamos; y así, consolando yo a Zoraida, atendimos todos a nuestro viaje, el cual nos le facilitaba el proprio viento, de tal manera que bien tuvimos por cierto de vernos otro día al amanecer en las riberas de España.
t: She said this at a moment when neither her father could hear her nor we could see her; and so, as I was consoling Zoraida, we all attended to our voyage, which the wind itself made easy for us, in such a way that we counted it certain that we would see each other again at daybreak on the shores of Spain.

o: »Habíanse puesto a bordo del bajel a preguntarnos quién éramos, y adónde navegábamos, y de dónde veníamos; pero, por preguntarnos esto en lengua francesa, dijo nuestro renegado: ''Ninguno responda; porque éstos, sin duda, son cosarios franceses, que hacen a toda ropa''.
t: "They had boarded the ship to ask us who we were, where we were sailing, and where we came from; but since they asked us this in the French tongue, our renegade said: 'Let no one answer; for these are undoubtedly French corsairs, who prey on everything.'

o: Amainaron entonces, y, echando el esquife o barca a la mar, entraron en él hasta doce franceses bien armados, con sus arcabuces y cuerdas encendidas, y así llegaron junto al nuestro; y, viendo cuán pocos éramos y cómo el bajel se hundía, nos recogieron, diciendo que, por haber usado de la descortesía de no respondelles, nos había sucedido aquello.
t: They then furled their sails, and launching the skiff or boat into the sea, up to twelve well-armed Frenchmen entered it, with theirarquebuses and lighted matches, and thus they came alongside our ship; and seeing how few we were and how our vessel was sinking, they took us aboard, saying that because we had used the discourtesy of not answering them, that had happened to us.

o: Nuestro renegado tomó el cofre de las riquezas de Zoraida, y dio con él en la mar, sin que ninguno echase de ver en lo que hacía.
t: Our renegade took the chest of Zoraida's riches and threw it into the sea, without anyone seeming to notice what he was doing.

o: En resolución, todos pasamos con los franceses, los cuales, después de haberse informado de todo aquello que de nosotros saber quisieron, como si fueran nuestros capitales enemigos, nos despojaron de todo cuanto teníamos, y a Zoraida le quitaron hasta los carcajes que traía en los pies.
t: In short, we all passed over to the Frenchmen, who, after learning everything they wished to know about us, as if they were our chief enemies, stripped us of everything we had, and they took from Zoraida even the shackles she wore on her feet.

o: Pero no me daba a mí tanta pesadumbre la que a Zoraida daban, como me la daba el temor que tenía de que habían de pasar del quitar de las riquísimas y preciosísimas joyas al quitar de la joya que más valía y ella más estimaba.
t: But what weighed on me was not so much what weighed on Zoraida as the fear I had that they would go on from taking away her richest and most precious jewels to taking away the jewel that was worth most and that she treasured most.

o: Pero los deseos de aquella gente no se estienden a más que al dinero, y desto jamás se vee harta su codicia; lo cual entonces llegó a tanto, que aun hasta los vestidos de cautivos nos quitaran si de algún provecho les fueran.
t: But the desires of that people extend no further than money, and their greed is never seen satisfied; which then reached such a point that they would even have stripped us of our clothes if those could be of any profit to them.

o: Y hubo parecer entre ellos de que a todos nos arrojasen a la mar envueltos en una vela, porque tenían intención de tratar en algunos puertos de España con nombre de que eran bretones, y si nos llevaban vivos, serían castigados, siendo descubierto su hurto.
t: And it was their opinion that they should throw us all into the sea wrapped in a sail, because they intended to trade in some ports of Spain under the name of being Bretons, and if they carried us off alive, they would be punished once their theft was discovered.

o: »Cerca de mediodía podría ser cuando nos echaron en la barca, dándonos dos barriles de agua y algún bizcocho; y el capitán, movido no sé de qué misericordia, al embarcarse la hermosísima Zoraida, le dio hasta cuarenta escudos de oro, y no consintió que le quitasen sus soldados estos mesmos vestidos que ahora tiene puestos.
t: "It was around noon when they threw us into the boat, giving us two barrels of water and some biscuit; and the captain, moved by some mercy I know not, on seeing the beautiful Zoraida board, gave her as much as forty gold escudos, and would not allow his soldiers to take from her the very garments she now wears.

o: Pero, de los contrarios pareceres, el que se tomó fue que nos llegásemos poco a poco, y que si el sosiego del mar lo concediese, desembarcásemos donde pudiésemos.
t: But of the conflicting opinions, the one that was taken was that we should make our way slowly along the coast, and that if the calm of the sea allowed it, we should land wherever we could.

o: »Hízose así, y poco antes de la media noche sería cuando llegamos al pie de una disformísima y alta montaña, no tan junto al mar que no concediese un poco de espacio para poder desembarcar cómodamente.
t: "So it was done, and it was a little before midnight when we arrived at the foot of a most misshapen and high mountain, not so close to the sea that it did not leave a little space to land comfortably.

o: Embestimos en la arena, salimos a tierra, besamos el suelo, y, con lágrimas de muy alegrísimo contento, dimos todos gracias a Dios, Señor Nuestro, por el bien tan incomparable que nos había hecho.
t: We ran her onto the sand, stepped ashore, kissed the ground, and all of us gave thanks to God, our Lord, with tears of the most joyful gladness, for the incomparable good he had done us.

o: Sacamos de la barca los bastimentos que tenía, tirámosla en tierra, y subímonos un grandísimo trecho en la montaña, porque aún allí estábamos, y aún no podíamos asegurar el pecho, ni acabábamos de creer que era tierra de cristianos la que ya nos sostenía.
t: We took out of the boat the gear it held, dragged it ashore, and climbed a very long stretch up the mountain, for we were still there, and could not yet be sure of our footing, nor quite believe that the land now bearing us was land of Christians.

o: Amaneció más tarde, a mi parecer, de lo que quisiéramos.
t: Daybreak came later, it seemed to me, than we would have wished.

o: Acabamos de subir toda la montaña, por ver si desde allí algún poblado se descubría, o algunas cabañas de pastores; pero, aunque más tendimos la vista, ni poblado, ni persona, ni senda, ni camino descubrimos.
t: We finished climbing the whole mountain, to see if from there some settlement might come into view, or some shepherds' huts; but, though we strained our eyes, we discovered neither settlement nor person, nor path nor road.

o: Con todo esto, determinamos de entrarnos la tierra adentro, pues no podría ser menos sino que presto descubriésemos quien nos diese noticia della.
t: All the same, we resolved to go inland, for it could not be otherwise than that we would soon discover someone who could give us news of it.

o: ¡Moros, moros! ¡Arma, arma!''
t: "Moors, moors! To arms, to arms!"

o: »Luego que los jinetes entendieron que éramos cristianos cautivos, se apearon de sus caballos, y cada uno nos convidaba con el suyo para llevarnos a la ciudad de Vélez Málaga, que legua y media de allí estaba.
t: As soon as the riders learned that we were Christian captives, they dismounted from their horses, and each of us was invited to mount with him and be taken to the city of Vélez-Málaga, a league and a half from there.

o: Algunos dellos volvieron a llevar la barca a la ciudad, diciéndoles dónde la habíamos dejado; otros nos subieron a las ancas, y Zoraida fue en las del caballo del tío del cristiano.
t: Some of them took the boat back to the city, telling them where we had left it; others set us behind them on their saddles, and Zoraida rode on the horse of the Christian's uncle.

o: Saliónos a recebir todo el pueblo, que ya de alguno que se había adelantado sabían la nueva de nuestra venida.
t: The whole town came out to receive us, for they had already learned from one who had gone ahead the news of our arrival.

o: »Fuimos derechos a la iglesia, a dar gracias a Dios por la merced recebida; y, así como en ella entró Zoraida, dijo que allí había rostros que se parecían a los de Lela Marién.
t: We went straight to the church, to give thanks to God for the mercy received; and as Zoraida entered it, she said that there were faces there that resembled Lela Marién's.

o: Dijímosle que eran imágines suyas, y como mejor se pudo le dio el renegado a entender lo que significaban, para que ella las adorase como si verdaderamente fueran cada una dellas la misma Lela Marién que la había hablado.
t: We told her they were images of her, and as best he could the renegade made her understand what they meant, so that she might worship them as if each of them truly were the very Lela Marién who had spoken with her.

o: Ella, que tiene buen entendimiento y un natural fácil y claro, entendió luego cuanto acerca de las imágenes se le dijo.
t: She, who had sound understanding and an easy, clear disposition, immediately grasped everything that had been said to her about the images.

o: Desde allí nos llevaron y repartieron a todos en diferentes casas del pueblo; pero al renegado, Zoraida y a mí nos llevó el cristiano que vino con nosotros, y en casa de sus padres, que medianamente eran acomodados de los bienes de fortuna, y nos regalaron con tanto amor como a su mismo hijo.
t: From there they took us and distributed us all among different houses in the village; but the renegade, Zoraida, and I were taken by the Christian who came with us, to his parents' house, who were moderately well provided with worldly goods, and they treated us with as much love as if we had been their own son.

o: No tengo más, señores, que deciros de mi historia; la cual, si es agradable y peregrina, júzguenlo vuestros buenos entendimientos; que de mí sé decir que quisiera habérosla contado más brevemente, puesto que el temor de enfadaros más de cuatro circustancias me ha quitado de la lengua.
t: I have nothing more, gentlemen, to tell you about my story; and if it is agreeable and full of marvels, let your good judgment decide; for of myself I can say that I would have told it to you more briefly, since the fear of offending you in more than four particulars has taken it from my tongue.
